description: Send a message to Anon, the Hey Anon on-chain AI agent (balances, swaps, bridging, lending, staking, CEX, scheduled automations, research). Asynchronous: the output is only a confirmation with the background task ID; poll background_task with that ID until status is no longer "pending" ("completed": the reply is in result; any other status, e.g. "failed": the request did not finish, check logs). Anon keeps NO conversation context: every message is processed from a clean slate, so each message must be self-contained (repeat the wallet, network, token and amount every time; follow-ups like "and on Base?" will not work). Before sending, the tool checks that Anon is idle: if the previous request is still processing it returns an error, poll background_task until it finishes (or call abort) and retry. Anon can execute real transactions from the attached wallets: send action instructions (swap, send, bridge, stake, create an automation) only when the user explicitly asked for that action, and phrase everything else as a question. For general crypto research not tied to the user wallets, prefer ask_gemma.

files.description: Optional attachments (publicly reachable URL + MIME type), e.g. a screenshot or document for Anon to analyze

text.description: Natural-language message or instruction for Anon. Phrase information requests as questions, e.g. "What is my S balance on Sonic?" or "Show my Aave positions". Action instructions such as "Swap 10 USDC to ETH on Base" can make Anon execute a real transaction from the attached wallet: send them only when the user explicitly requested that exact action, token and amount

wallets.description: Wallet addresses to attach: at least one, and at most ONE per wallet type (e.g. one evm, one solana, one ton). Two addresses of the same type are rejected by the backend ("Multiple wallets found for type evm"). Take addresses from wallet_list. If the user has several wallets of the same type, use the one the user named (by displayName or address); otherwise ask which one to use rather than picking arbitrarily.
